preconditions.description: The first line contains an integer K, and the second line contains exactly K space-separated integers.
The size of the permutation K is between 1 and 100 inclusive.
The permutation P contains exactly the numbers from 1 to K with no duplicates.

preconditions.expression: len(adj_matrix) == K and all(len(row) == K for row in adj_matrix)
preconditions.description: The adjacency matrix consists of K lines, each containing exactly K characters.

preconditions.expression: all(c in 'YN' for row in adj_matrix for c in row)
preconditions.description: Each character in the adjacency matrix is either 'Y' or 'N'.

preconditions.expression: all(adj_matrix[i][j] == adj_matrix[j][i] for i in range(K) for j in range(K))
preconditions.description: The exchange relation is symmetric (if i can swap with j, j can swap with i).

postconditions.description: The output permutation contains exactly the same elements as the input permutation.

postconditions.expression: all(result_values[i] in component_values[i] for i in range(K))
postconditions.description: For every position i, the value placed there belongs to the set of values originally present in the connected component containing i.

postconditions.expression: all(sorted(result_values[i] for i in component_indices[c]) == sorted(P[i] for i in component_indices[c]) for c in components)
postconditions.description: Within each connected component of indices, the multiset of values assigned to those positions matches the multiset of values originally at those positions.

postconditions.expression: all(result_values[i] == min(available_values[i]) for i in range(K))
postconditions.description: The resulting permutation is lexicographically smallest: for each position i, the value assigned is the smallest available value from the connected component of i that has not been used in any position j < i belonging to the same component.
The output is formatted as K space-separated integers on a single line.
